items.abstract: <jats:p>Purpose: Work-related stress among midwives results in secondary traumatic stress, posttraumatic stress disorder, and job attrition. The purpose of this pilot project was to evaluate the effectiveness of a holistic, web-based program using holistic modalities for stress reduction and improved coping among certified nurse-midwives. Design and Method: A convenience sample of 10 midwives participated in a web-based holistic stress reduction intervention using yoga, mindfulness-based stress reduction, and meditation for four days each week over 4 weeks. Participants completed pre- and postintervention questionnaires (Perceived Stress Scale [PSS] and the Coping Self-Efficacy Scale [CSES]) for evaluation of effectiveness. Findings: The PSS means showed improvement in midwives’ stress (16.4-12.3). The CSES means showed improvement in coping (174.8-214.5). Improvement was shown in each subscale of the CSES (“uses problem-focused coping”: 19.2%; “stops unpleasant thoughts and emotions”: 20.3%; and “gets support from family and friends”: 16.6%). Conclusion: Findings suggest the potential for stress reduction and improved coping skills after using holistic techniques in a web-based format within a cohort of nurse-midwives. Further research of web-based, holistic intervention for stress reduction among midwives is warranted.</jats:p>
title: Evaluation of a Web-Based Holistic Stress Reduction Pilot Program Among Nurse-Midwives

items.abstract: <jats:p>Safe and efficient airport surface operations underpin the resilience of global air transportation. Yet, airport visual surveillance remains largely perception-centric, delivering object locations and tracks while providing limited support for understanding what multiple heterogeneous objects are doing over time. We therefore study Multi-Object Action Modeling for airport visual surveillance, which progressively integrates detection, tracking, and captioning to produce ID-aligned and temporally coherent operational captions under long-range imaging constraints. To enable rigorous and comparable evaluation, we introduce Air-SMOAM, a semantic-enhanced benchmark that couples long-horizon tracks with schema-constrained, frame-level action captions and supports a window-level inference protocol with window-to-frame evaluation. Air-SMOAM reflects procedure-driven apron operations and the practical challenges of distant wide-field cameras, including pervasive small objects, extreme scale variation, occlusion, and background clutter. Moreover, motivated by recent advances in vision-language models that map object-centric visual evidence to structured language, we present Air-TraLVLM, a strong baseline that optimizes LVLM prompting on track-conditioned evidence and generates temporally stable action semantics. On the Air-SMOAM test set, Air-TraLVLM achieves 0.776 Full Accuracy and 8.143 CIDEr, while maintaining high temporal coherence with 0.064 Flicker and 0.737 Longest Correct Streak Ratio. Together, Air-SMOAM and Air-TraLVLM establish a principled foundation for semantic-enhanced airport visual surveillance.</jats:p>
title: Semantic Enhanced Multi-Object Action Modeling Benchmark and LVLM Prompt Optimization for Airport Visual Surveillance
